rationale: The original prostate trial reports dizziness in 2 of 34 tamsulosin participants and none of 39 pumpkin oil participants. No placebo, verified grade, standing trigger or Parkinson cohort.
The already tracked Karli/NCT07123844 article records seated blood pressure endpoints without arm-specific values in the abstract. The main clinical table remains open.

The preprint compares commercial pumpkin and red palm oils in an induced hypertension rat model. Orthostatic and symptom outcomes are unmeasured. Compare lineage with the related 2025 journal report before counting separately.
The clinical oil trial reports within-arm resting brachial and central systolic changes. Full comparative figures and a standing symptom endpoint remain unverified.
The clinical intervention is extracted squalene administered sublingually in COVID-19. Baseline hypertension is a cohort characteristic and no culinary oil or orthostatic symptom is compared.
Oral oil and amlodipine arms assess arterial pressure in rats with induced hypertension. The abstract gives no postural or clinical dizziness outcome.
Pumpkin oil is part of a multi-ingredient quercetin-delivery vehicle in a rodent metabolic model. It does not give the isolated oil or lightheadedness contrast.
The previously cataloged pilot reports resting diastolic pressure and no established orthostatic symptom endpoint. The 12-week arm difference is inconclusive.
Pretreatment with pumpkin oil in spontaneously hypertensive rats altered the blood pressure response after intravenous felodipine or captopril. No postural symptom test.
Pumpkin oil versus corn oil is compared for pressure and lipids in ovariectomized and non-ovariectomized female rats. There is no defined cold-pressed grade or standing symptom.
Original whole-celery methanol-extract mouse study measures motor behavior. Hallucinations are mentioned as medication background, without dried leaf or visual frequency measurement.
All four original printed pages describe a mixed historical product and uncontrolled cases. No verified dried leaf or visual hallucination count. Dried leaves refer to coca.
